host.description:
The URL of your dedicated Lucca account: `{account}.{env}.{region}`.

Account reflects your company name. Env indicates the environment. Region depends on your server location.

**Please, use your test or sandbox environments (and not your production env.) for testing purposes.**

Environments:
- `ilucca`: production environment for customers.
- `ilucca-test`: test environment for customers.
- `ilucca-demo`: demo environment for prospects.

Regions:
- `.ch` for Swiss located accounts.
- `.net` for the others.

Regarding sandboxes, the pattern differs: `https://{account}-{sandboxName}.sandbox.{server}.luccasoftware.com`, where:
- `{sandboxName}` is automatically generated upon creation.
- `{server}` may be "eu1", "eu2" or "ch1".

events endpoint, or they can be sent to your webhook-endpoint.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique id of the file.

get.description: Retrieve a file, either its JSON representation or its content.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description:
The token allowing to access the file, required in addition to the access token: the access token lets you use the files API, and this token, minted by the service that owns the file, lets you view this file.
This token can only be obtained via the API resource that references this file, read with `?include=links`: `links.files["{id}"].token` (e.g. on an employee-attribute, an employment, a job-position or an employee).
It is bound to the API client that read the resource, and expires after `links.files["{id}"].expiresAt`. The deprecated `links.document` and `links.portrait` links also carry one, whose expiry is not exposed.

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description:
The **Accept** response header indicates the content type of the response.

- `Accept: application/octet-stream` returns the raw file content.
- `Accept: image/*` returns a preview of the file (when possible).
- If Accept matches exactly `file.contentType`, returns the raw file content.
- `Accept: application/json` or `Accept: */*` or no Accept header (default) returns the file metadata in JSON format.

parameters.name: disposition
parameters.description:
Specifies how the file should be handled by the client.

Supersedes the `Accept` header when possible. To be used whenever the API client cannot set custom `Accept` headers.

- `json` (default) returns the file metadata in JSON format.
- `inline` returns the file content to be displayed inline in the browser (when possible).
- `attachment` returns the file content as a download.

200.description: Representation of the requested file, either its JSON representation or its content.

401.description:
You are not authenticated: the `Authorization` header is missing, or the access token is invalid or expired.
The `token` query parameter does not authenticate you on its own.

403.description:
You may not access this file: your access token lacks the `files.readonly` or `files.readwrite` scope, or the
`token` query parameter is missing, expired, or was minted for another API client.

put.description:
Replace an employee-attribute-definition.

Only the extensions created by your organization can be updated: any other definition returns a `400` with the `attribute-definition-not-editable` error. The base schema of `schema` cannot change.

Unlike `PATCH`, the request body replaces the whole definition: an omitted `isArchived` unarchives it, an omitted `multipleValueHandling` makes it single-valued, and omitted translations are removed.

Example request body, with a `schema` referencing a Lucca base schema:

```json
{
  "name": "T-shirt size",
  "multipleValueHandling": null,
  "schema": { "$ref": "/lucca-api/schemas/taxonomy-label-reference" },
  "isArchived": false,
  "t9n": { "name": { "fr-FR": "Taille de t-shirt" } }
}
```

Languages are identified through their RFC 4646 language tag.

legal-entity.title: legal-entity
legal-entity.description:
Representation of a legal entity, i.e. an organization that is subject to legal responsibilities in a given jurisdiction (country).

A legal-entity may be comprised of several [business-establishments](/api-reference/2024-11-01/organization/business-establishment) which represent geographically localized structures where the actual work is done. One of which is marked as the legal-entity headquarters.

legalName.description: **Must be unique**. Legal name of the legal-entity.

remoteId.description: The third-party API ID of the matching object.

isArchived.description: If this legal-entity is archived. Only possible if there are no more business-establishment attached.

taxIdentificationNumber.description:
Identifier of the legal-entity in its local jurisdiction.
- France: SIREN (Système d'identification du répertoire des entreprises)
- Germany: SN (Steuernummer).
- Spain: N.I.F (Número de Identificación Fiscal)

industryCode.description:
The industry (classification) code identifies the main type of activity of this legal-entity.
- France: APE or NAF code.
- Spain: CNAE.
- Germany: WZ (Die Klassifikation der Wirtschaftszweige).
- U.S.A.: NAICS (North American Industry Classification System).

page-link.title: page-link
page-link.description:

Follow `href` as is, or call the same operation with `cursor` as its `page` query parameter, and the same other
query parameters as the current request (filters, `limit`, `include`).

cursor.description:
The `page` query parameter of `href`: an opaque cursor, exposed on its own so that clients and tools can
request the page through the operation, without parsing `href`.

prev.description:
Link to the previous page, or `null` when there is none.
It may be set on the first page, and then leads to an empty page.

next.description:
Link to the next page, or `null` when there is none: stop paging when `next` is `null`.
It may be set on the last page when that page is full, and then leads to an empty page whose `next` is `null`.

embedded.description: No embedded resources on a legal-entity(ies) response. Expect an empty object if embedded are requested.

addressLines.description:
Unstructured ordered address lines describing the lower levels of an address.
Empty when the address has no lines.

postalCode.description:
Optional. Postal code of the address. Not all countries use or require 
postal codes to be present, but where they are used, they may trigger 
additional validation with other parts of the address 
(e.g. city validation).

locality.description:
Optional. Generally refers to the city/town portion of the address.

administrativeArea.description:

addresses of a country or region. For example, this can be a state, 
a province, an oblast, or a prefecture.

business-establishment.title: business-establishment
business-establishment.description:
A business-establishment is a geographically localized unit of the organization structure.

It belongs to a [legal-entity](/api-reference/2024-11-01/organization/legal-entity). A legal-entity may have one (and only one) business-establishment set as its headquarters.

Business-establishments are an essential resource of the enterprise model, as they are the fundamental units of access rights scoping. As such, most objects are either directly or indirectly attached to a business-establishment.

Employees are attached to a business-establishment through their job-position.

remoteId.description: The third-party API ID of the matching object.

isArchived.description: If this business-establishment is archived. Only possible if there are no more employees attached.

legalEntity.description: Reference to the [legal-entity](/api-reference/2024-11-01/organization/legal-entity) this business-establishment belongs to.

isHeadquarters.description:
True when this business-establishment should be considered the headquarters of the legal-entity it belongs to.
A legal-entity may only have a single one headquarters.

taxIdentificationNumber.description: - France: SIRET (Système d'identification du répertoire des établissements). Must start with the same identifier than its legal-entity (SIREN).

industryCode.description:
The industry (classification) code identifies the main type of activity of this legal-entity.
- France: APE or NAF code.
- Spain: CNAE.
- Germany: WZ (Die Klassifikation der Wirtschaftszweige).
- U.S.A.: NAICS (North American Industry Classification System).

totalCount.description: Total number of business-establishment resources across all pages that satisfy query parameters.

embedded.description:
Embeds the representation of resources related to the business-establishment(s).

Only returned if requested by the API client: `?include=embedded`.

legal-entity.description:
Legal-entities the business-establishment(s) belong to (cf. `businessEstablishment.legalEntity`).

Structured as a dictionary of [legal-entities](/api-reference/2024-11-01/organization/legal-entity) indexed by ID.

department.title: department
department.description:
A department represents a subdivision of the employee workforce, most often erected around 
the type of activity they do.

Departments are a tree-like structure, as any department may be child to another.

Note: contrary to most resources, departments are not attached to business-establishments.
This means:
  - business-establishments listed in access rights management do not affect departments.
  - employees may work in different business-establishments (or even legal-entities) and yet
    still belong to the same department.

remoteId.description: Identifier of this object in a third-party software.

isArchived.description: If this department is archived. Only possible if there are no more employees attached.

parent.description: Reference to the department this department is a child of.

manager.description: Reference to the employee that acts as the Head of this department.

sortOrder.description: Index (0-based) of the department among its siblings.

owningApplication.description:
**Can only be set by an authenticated Lucca application.** 
When not null, indicates that this department is read-only, given that it is managed by another application (designated by its ID) that is charged with its synchronization.
**Any write request attempt made from anyone other than the application will be rejected with a 403 Forbidden error.**

activeEmployees.description: Link to the paginated list of active employees currently positioned in this department. List may be partial due to insufficient access rights.

occupation-category.title: occupation-category
occupation-category.description:
The occupation-category resource represents a categorization of employees belonging to a set of business-establishments.

These categories can be used as a way of distinguishing employees in reports, or may be used to specify reserved business rules (e.g. in the leaves management system).

In France, can be used to represent the "Profession et Catégories Professionnelles" (P.C.S.).

job-qualification.title: job-qualification
job-qualification.description:
A job-qualification is an object that represents an employee profile regarding their skillset.

It is composed of both:
- a [profession](/api-reference/2024-11-01/employee-job-qualifications/profession), which indicates the nature of their job.
- a rank (number), which indicates either their level of expertise or of responsibilities in the company.

rank.description: The lower the rank, the "lower" in the company's hierarchy (i.e. the CEO is at max rank). Maximum rank can be set trough configuration.

- upcoming: employee currently has no employment but will have one in the future.
- deactivated: employee used to have an employment but no longer does.

applicability.description:
The time window during which this attribute value applies to the employee.

Two periods are exposed side by side:

- `start` / `end` describe the **computed** period. It is stretched to cover the gaps between two consecutive resources, so that the history of an attribute reads as an uninterrupted timeline. As a result it may span periods during which the employee had no contract at all.
- `strictStart` / `strictEnd` describe the **strict** period, inherited from the source resource (`employment`, `job-position`) without any gap filling. Use it whenever contractual accuracy matters, typically to build point-in-time reports.

A `null` lower bound must be interpreted as "since the beginning of time", and a `null` upper bound as "until the end of time".

If the attribute has no temporal dimension (e.g. `employee.givenName`, `e_tShirtSize`), all four dates are `null`. It must be interpreted as "applies indefinitely".

The `applicability.asOf` and `applicability.strictAsOf` query parameters can be used to filter by date, on the computed and on the strict period respectively.

start.description: Inclusive lower bound of the computed period, which fills the gaps between consecutive resources. Null means no lower limit ("since the beginning of time").

end.description: Inclusive upper bound of the computed period, which fills the gaps between consecutive resources. Null means no upper limit ("until the end of time").

strictStart.description: Inclusive lower bound of the strict period, inherited from the source resource without gap filling. Null means no lower limit ("since the beginning of time").

strictEnd.description: Inclusive upper bound of the strict period, inherited from the source resource without gap filling. Null means no upper limit ("until the end of time").

webhook-endpoint.description:
A webhook-endpoint describes the endpoint on your side that will receive events from your Lucca account.

It must handle HTTPS and support POST requests.

It should always check the signature of received events in order to increase security.

It should respond as fast as possible (less than 3s), otherwise the server may stop sending it events.

Please refer to the [webhooks documentation](/documentation/webhooks/get-started) to learn more about webhook-endpoints.
